newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFI share market seen shallow at start.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFI share market seen shallow at start.

text.p: Trade in National Investment Fund (NFI) shares will be possible when at least 20 percent of the units in Poland's mass privatisation scheme are exchanged for NFI shares, an NFI official said on Monday.
Rafal Zagorny, head of NFI No. 12 (Piast), said that below the 20 percent threshold, the volatility of prices of NFI shares would be too high for trade to be possible.

"For trade in NFI shares to be possible at least 20 percent of the units should be exchanged for shares in the funds. At first this market is likely to be very shallow," Zagorny told a news conference.

The head of Piast's management firm, Krzysztof Mikulski, told the conference that many investors who hold large portfolios of NFI units would likely hold back from exchanging them for NFI shares because the units were very liquid.

"There is a large group of investors, notably foreign ones, who are likely to hold back with exchanging their NFI certificates because they are a highly liquid instrument, while the value of the NFIs is still difficult to assess," he said.
Zagorny said that first quotes of NFI shares on the bourse might show large price differences between the funds.
"The fewer shares in trade, the larger the price differences will be," Zagorny said.

NFI units can be exchanged for NFI shares from May 12 until the end of 1998. Each unit will be exchanged for a total of 15 NFI shares -- one in each of the 15 funds created under the programme to run a total of 514 companies.
Bourse trade in NFI shares is likely to start in June.
